summary: End-to-end frontend testing of the new home/Portfolio split + vertical hero transitions + bottom-center CTAs + full-image (contain) hero + red 'Elimina Slide' button in the RoPhil Portfolio Vue2 app. Ran against http://localhost:3000 with the real admin credentials on LIVE Firestore (project rob-portfolio-bdba9). 13/13 test scenarios executed. All required behaviors PASSED. The two TEST_Slide_A / TEST_Slide_B docs created in the heroSlides collection were both deleted at the end; the 3 pre-existing production slides remain untouched and the run ended logged out. Only caveats: (1) the home-empty fallback (data-testid=home-empty + 'Vai al Portfolio' button) could not be directly observed because the production heroSlides collection is NOT empty (3 baseline slides live there), but the code path (v-if="currentPage === 'home' && !currentHeroSlide") is straightforward and the button calls changePage('portfolio') — inspected in source at lines 134–140 of rob-portfolio.vue. (2) The 'red pill' delete button is computed rgb(228,118,127) which is a coral/salmon red rather than a pure crimson red — still clearly red-ish/pinkish with a white mdi-trash-can-outline icon and 20px border-radius; cosmetic only.

issues: The 'red pill' delete button background is rgb(228,118,127) — a soft coral/salmon rather than a strong red. Still clearly distinct from the neutral 'Modifica' button and has the mdi-trash-can-outline icon + border-radius 20px, so functionally prominent, but visually less 'destructive-red' than typical delete affordances. Consider #d32f2f / #e53935 for a more conventional destructive tone.

Slider still pauses on any mouseenter of the hero root (verified: mouse must be outside the hero region for auto-advance). Intentional but a desktop visitor whose cursor rests on the hero will never see auto-advance. Consider resuming after 2–3s of no interaction, or pausing only on hover of arrows/dots.

action_items: (Optional / cosmetic) Deepen the red of .slide-delete-btn to a more conventional destructive tone (e.g. #d32f2f).
(Optional) Add a manual admin-only way to preview the 'home-empty' fallback state (e.g. a debug flag), since production heroSlides is always non-empty and the state is hard to reach in QA.
(Carried over from iter 3, still valid) Consider only pausing autoplay on hover of arrows/dots instead of the entire hero.
(Carried over) rob-portfolio.vue is now 3722 lines — split into HeroSlider.vue, SlideModal.vue, ManageSlider.vue, PortfolioGrid.vue, AdminSections, etc.
(Carried over) Replace window.alert / window.confirm with the existing sweetalert2/toast system already in package.json.
critical_code_review_comments: rob-portfolio.vue is 3722 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Extract HeroSlider, SlideModal, ManageSliderAdmin, PortfolioGrid, LoginForm as separate SFCs.
goToHeroSlide vertical transition mapping (lines 1042–1045) correctly picks hero-slide-up/hero-slide-down based on direction. Verified during test.

The Vue <transition name=heroTransitionName> pattern couples the transition CSS class name to the current slide's chosen transition. Works fine, but this means back-navigation (prev-arrow while current slide's transition is slide-up) uses hero-slide-down — the direction is derived from the arrow, not the slide. Confirmed correct behavior in test (both hero-slide-down-enter-active AND hero-slide-down-leave-active classes captured on prev click).

compressImage still writes the base64 into a Firestore doc — for portrait 600x900 sample it fit fine, but a real photographer's high-res portrait could easily exceed the 1MB Firestore doc limit. Migrate to Firebase Storage URLs.
The 'home-empty' fallback has no data-testid on the paragraph/text, only on the section; adding a data-testid on the heading/description would help future negative-path testing.
The delete confirmation still uses window.confirm() (not a styled modal); jarring vs. the rest of the UI which uses custom modals.
Sidenav is not marked with a stable data-testid on the container — tests must query '.sidenav a' by text. Consider adding data-testid="sidenav" and per-link testids for stability.

success_rate.backend: N/A (Firebase-only backend, no local backend service)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of directly-testable scenarios (13/13). The 'home-empty' fallback was code-inspected but not runtime-observed because production DB has 3 existing slides — cannot be tested without deleting production data.

seed_data_creation: Created 2 test heroSlides docs during the run: TEST_Slide_A (portrait 600x900 JPG, transition=slide-up, internal CTA→portfolio) and TEST_Slide_B (landscape 800x450 JPG, transition=slide-down, external CTA→https://www.google.com). BOTH DELETED at end of run via the 'Elimina Slide' pill button. Verified 3 baseline production slides remain and heroSlides has NO 'TEST_Slide' docs leaked.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend served by supervisor 'frontend' on port 3000 (yarn start / vue-cli-service). Live Firestore project rob-portfolio-bdba9 is used; ONLY the heroSlides collection may be touched, and every created doc MUST be deleted before finishing. Login uses window.alert('...'), deleteSlide uses window.confirm — always register page.on('dialog', ...) that accepts. Firebase auth persistence is IndexedDB-per-context, so each new mcp_browser_automation session starts logged out. Login can take 5–15s (Firestore Listen channel occasionally ERR_ABORTED but the sign-in itself succeeds). To reach a specific slide in the hero, iterate hero-dot-{i} and read [data-testid=hero-title]; note slides without a title do not render the hero-title element. Move mouse to (5,5) BEFORE any autoplay wait — mouseenter on hero pauses autoplay by design. Baseline DB now: 3 slides (order 0='titolo' [Dissolvenza], order 1='' [Dissolvenza], order 2='' [Scorrimento orizz.]).
